title: Ibrahim's du'a
hookLine: make me and my children keep the prayer, and accept my prayer (14:40)

lines: THE IDOLS, THE FIRE, THE VALLEY.
cards: Ibrahim has done almost everything a person of faith could do. He broke the idols. He walked out of the fire.

He left his wife and baby in an empty valley on Allah's word. With his son Isma'il, he raised the walls of the Ka'bah, stone by stone. If anyone had earned the right to feel sure of himself, it's him.
And at the end of his prayer in surah fourteen, he still asks to be kept, and to be accepted.

teach.h: KEEP ME, AND MY CHILDREN, PRAYING.
teach.b: Surah Ibrahim, verse forty, in Pickthall's translation: "My Lord! Make me to establish proper worship, and some of my posterity (also); our Lord! and accept the prayer." Two requests.
The first: make me keep up the prayer, me and my children after me. Not make me rich, not make me remembered. Keep me praying, and keep them praying.
He asks for himself first. Even Ibrahim doesn't assume he'll stay steady on his own.
The second is today's line: wa taqabbal du'a', and accept my prayer. Asking isn't the end of it. He asks for the asking to be received.
In the next verse he widens the circle: our Lord, forgive me, and my parents, and the believers, on the day the reckoning is set up. Here's the scholar's thread.
He says the same kind of thing in al-Baqarah, verse one twenty-seven, while the walls of the Ka'bah are going up: our Lord, accept from us.
Commentators record that an early pious man, Wuhayb ibn al-Ward, wept when he recited it: the Friend of the Merciful is building Allah's own House, and he's afraid it won't be accepted.
In both places, Ibrahim doesn't treat a good deed as finished just because it's done.
Some Muslims recite these verses, fourteen forty and forty-one, in the last sitting of their prayer, so the prayer ends asking for itself to be accepted.

how: Some Muslims recite Ibrahim's du'a (14:40–41) in the final sitting of the prayer, before the closing salam, asking for themselves, their children and their parents.

o: keep me and my children praying; accept it
a prayer for wealth for his descendants
thanks for being saved from the fire

p: make me and my children keep the prayer
forgive me, my parents, the believers

s: Ibrahim asked only for his children to keep the prayer
he asked for himself first: make me establish worship, and some of my offspring.
Ibrahim asked for acceptance while building the Ka'bah
Ibrahim's prayer in surah fourteen includes his parents
14:41: forgive me and my parents and the believers.

games.q: you've just finished building the Ka'bah with your son, at Allah's command. what do you pray?
o: make it the greatest house on earth.
games.why: Ibrahim and Isma'il ask for acceptance (2:127), and commentators record that an early pious man wept at it.

practice: Bring your family to mind one by one, parents, children, siblings, a partner, and picture each in a quiet moment of their own, praying, pausing, or looking for meaning in their way.
If you pray, ask for each by name, as Ibrahim did, that they keep their prayer, then add his last words: and accept my prayer. If you don't, simply wish each of them steadiness.

wordCard.voice: Ibrahim's du'a. Make me and my children keep the prayer, and accept my prayer: the builder of the Ka'bah, still asking to be accepted. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic, 14:40: our Lord, and accept my prayer.

carryVoice: Your line: accept my prayer. A good deed still asks to be received. Until tomorrow.

sources.q: My Lord! Make me to establish proper worship, and some of my posterity (also); our Lord! and accept the prayer.

sources.ref: Wuhayb ibn al-Ward on 2:127 (reported in Ibn Kathir's tafsir)
